mainTopic: ברירה in rabbinic law (הלכה like רבי אושעיא), and whose 'feet' animals, borrowed כלים and borrowed ingredients follow on יום טוב
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of ברירה, the idea that a later event can show what was chosen from the start. The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה, because he explained איו's ברייתא as a case where the חכם had already arrived. So the גמרא does not switch the opinions. Instead it explains that רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה only in Torah law and accepts it in rabbinic law. מר זוטרא rules that the הלכה follows רבי אושעיא. Next, שמואל teaches that a fattener's ox may go wherever its future buyer may go, but a shepherd's ox follows only the people of his town. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules about a borrowed כלי. If the loan was set before יום טוב, the כלי follows the borrower. If the loan was made on יום טוב, it follows the lender, even when the borrower borrows from him regularly. Finally, רבי אבא arrives in ארץ ישראל and finds sages asking why the borrowed water and salt are not nullified in the dough. His answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Recalling the question on איו's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back an old question: if two-sages-in-two-places fails because there is no ברירה, the one-sage-east-or-west case should fail too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: What is different about 'here and there' (two sages), where it does not work because there is no ברירה? In 'east and west' (one sage) there is also no ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a question it once asked about the ברייתא of איו. This is setting up the next move, a challenge to switching the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איו's ברייתא, רבי יהודה lets a person put down two עירובין and later follow whichever direction the one sage went. But he does not allow this when two sages come to two places. If the two-sage case fails because there is no ברירה, the one-sage case should fail for the same reason, since there too the person only finds out later.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we raised a question about it)
Retroactive choice: deciding later which option counted from the start

phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא of איו about a person who puts down two עירובין, one on each side of town.

phrases.english: What is different about 'here and here,' that it does not work
— because there is no retroactive choice,
in east and west there is also no retroactive choice!
phrases.notes: East and west is the case of one sage whose direction isn't known yet. There, the ברייתא says it works.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא לְכָאן וּלְכָאן דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Recalls an earlier discussion to build a challenge against switching the opinions of רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's distinction in איו's ברייתא between one sage (east or west) and two sages (here and here).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two-sage case fails for lack of ברירה, the one-sage case should fail too, since both depend on information known only later.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the sage had already arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in the east/west case the sage had already arrived before שבת. The facts were already set, and only the person did not know them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The sage had already come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the old question. In the one-sage case, the sage was already in town before the עירוב took effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sage was already in one place, the right עירוב was set from the start. The person simply didn't know which one it was. So this case does not depend on ברירה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Food placed to extend one's Shabbat walking area

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּכְבָר בָּא חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the recalled question by redefining the one-sage case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the outcome was already set, just unknown)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The east/west case needs ברירה just like the two-sage case.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the east/west case the sage had already arrived, so no ברירה is needed.

steps.title: So רבי יוחנן does not hold of ברירה
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's answer, the גמרא concludes that he rejects ברירה even in a rabbinic matter like עירוב. That undercuts the switch of opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows that רבי יוחנן does not hold of ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's answer and uses it as a challenge. It shows that switching the opinions does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן accepted ברירה, he would not have needed to say the sage had already come. Since עירוב is rabbinic, this shows he rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law. So the switched version, where רבי יוחנן holds of ברירה, falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of (does not accept)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan does not hold of retroactive choice!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא: לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יוחנן's answer into evidence against switching the opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier proposal to switch (איפוך) the opinions so that רבי יוחנן holds of ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן needed the sage to have already come, which shows he rejects ברירה even in rabbinic matters.

steps.title: Don't switch: רבי אושעיא splits Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the original opinions. רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה only in Torah matters but accepts it in rabbinic ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: really, do not switch them. When does רבי אושעיא not hold of ברירה? In Torah law. But in rabbinic law, he does hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the switch and goes back to the original opinions. It solves the original contradiction in רבי אושעיא with a new distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source showing רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה is about a Torah law. His ruling that relies on ברירה is about a rabbinic matter. So both statements fit: ברירה is not used in דאורייתא but is used in דרבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law. רבי אושעיא rejects it in Torah law but accepts it in rabbinic law.
steps.confusionAlert: "Don't switch" means we go back to the original attributions. It is not a new switch.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule used all over שס: ברירה can work for rabbinic laws even if it does not work for Torah laws.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרֵירָה
phrases.english: and when Rabbi Oshaya does not hold of retroactive choice
but in rabbinic law — he does hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by dropping the switch and limiting רבי אושעיא's rejection of ברירה to Torah law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction (Torah law versus rabbinic law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה everywhere, so the opinions must be switched.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אושעיא rejects ברירה only in Torah law and accepts it in rabbinic law, so no switch is needed.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the הלכה follows רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא publicly rules like רבי אושעיא, so ברירה works in rabbinic matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught publicly: The הלכה is like רבי אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends with a practical ruling. The הלכה follows רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אושעיא accepts ברירה in rabbinic law, the practical ruling is that ברירה works there. It does not work in Torah law.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רבי אושעיא: in rabbinic matters we rely on ברירה.
steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after רבי אושעיא's view has been clarified.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אושעיא: ברירה works in rabbinic matters.

steps.title: שמואל: the fattener's ox and the shepherd's ox
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a fattener's ox follows the feet of anyone who buys it, while a shepherd's ox follows the feet of the people of his own city.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: An ox belonging to a fattener is like the feet of every person. An ox belonging to a shepherd is like the feet of the people of that city.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule about where an animal that is for sale may be taken on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object may only go where its owner may walk on יום טוב, which is called its owner's 'feet'. A fattener sells to anyone, so when יום טוב begins he has in mind whoever ends up buying, and the ox follows that buyer. A shepherd only sells now and then to local people, so his ox may go only where the people of his town may go.

keyTerms.meaning: A fattener, someone whose business is fattening oxen to sell them for meat
A shepherd who raises animals for himself and only sometimes sells them
'Like the feet of'. The object may go only where that person may walk on יום טוב
The boundary area a person or object may move within on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the owner's intention when יום טוב begins decides whose 'feet' an object follows.

phrases.english: is like the feet of every person.
phrases.notes: It can go wherever the person who buys it on יום טוב may go, even if the buyer is from another town.

phrases.english: is like the feet of that city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after ruling like רבי אושעיא (ברירה works in rabbinic matters), the גמרא brings שמואל's rule. It fits that idea: the fattener's ox follows a buyer who only becomes known later, on יום טוב, and תחומין are a rabbinic matter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fattener's ox follows the feet of whoever buys it. A shepherd's ox follows the feet of the people of the shepherd's city.

steps.title: Why say that a כלי borrowed before יום טוב follows the borrower?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כלי borrowed on ערב יום טוב and asks why it needs to be said, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One who borrows a כלי from his friend on ערב יום טוב, it follows the borrower's feet. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and asks why the משנה needed to teach something so plain. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone borrowed a כלי before יום טוב, it was already in his hands when יום טוב began. Of course it should follow his feet. So why did the משנה bother to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: 'It's obvious!' The גמרא asks why something needed to be said

phrases.english: One who borrows a vessel from his friend
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which ends 'it is like the feet of the borrower'.

phrases.english: on the eve of Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves from שמואל's rule to explaining a line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a כלי borrowed on ערב יום טוב follows the borrower
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The borrower already had the כלי when יום טוב began, so the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: The case where the כלי was only handed over on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the borrowing was arranged before יום טוב but the כלי was only handed over on יום טוב. It still follows the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed where the lender only handed it over on יום טוב. You might have said: since he did not put it in the borrower's possession before יום טוב, it should follow the lender. So the משנה teaches us that it follows the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a less obvious case. The borrowing was agreed on before יום טוב, but the כלי was physically given only on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that a כלי still with the lender when יום טוב began stays tied to the lender's feet. The משנה teaches that agreeing to the loan before יום טוב is enough. The כלי follows the borrower even though he only received it later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed, except...' The opening of an answer that points to a less obvious case
'You might have said.' This is the mistaken thought the ruling comes to correct

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרוֹ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: where he did not hand it over to him until Yom Tov.
he did not place it in his possession,
phrases.notes: Meaning the lender had not yet put it in the borrower's hands before יום טוב, so it should still follow the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרוֹ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a less obvious case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כלי not yet handed over before יום טוב stays tied to the lender's feet.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the loan was agreed on before יום טוב, the כלי follows the borrower even if he received it on יום טוב.

steps.title: The משנה supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Read this way, the משנה supports רבי יוחנן, who said this exact ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן, for רבי יוחנן said: One who borrows a כלי from his friend on ערב יום טוב, even if the lender only gave it to him on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the way it just explained the משנה matches a teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ruled that the time the loan is agreed on decides, not the time the כלי is handed over. The explanation in step 8 says the same thing. So the משנה backs up רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It supports him.' A source backs up someone's opinion

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי borrowed before יום טוב follows the borrower's feet, even if he only received it on יום טוב (רבי יוחנן, supported by the משנה).

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One who borrows a vessel from his friend on the eve of Yom Tov,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נְתָנוֹ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: even though he did not give it to him until Yom Tov,
it is like the feet of the borrower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the explanation in step 8 matches רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a כלי borrowed on ערב יום טוב but handed over on יום טוב follows the borrower
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, read as in step 8

steps.title: Why say that a כלי borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a כלי borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender. It asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If he borrowed on יום טוב, the כלי is like the feet of the lender. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second line of the משנה and again asks why something so plain needed saying. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב began, the כלי still belonged to the lender, and nothing had been arranged with the borrower yet. So of course it is tied to the lender's feet. The משנה seems to add nothing.

phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה again: if he borrowed on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: it is like the feet of the lender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה and asks the same kind of question as step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a כלי borrowed on יום טוב follows the lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כלי was fully the lender's when יום טוב began, so the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: Even a regular borrower: the lender might expect him to go elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a borrower who regularly borrows from this lender. Even so, the כלי follows the lender, because the lender thinks the borrower might borrow from someone else this time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed where he regularly borrows from him. You might have said that the lender already sets the כלי aside for him. So the משנה teaches us that it follows the lender, because the lender says to himself: maybe he will find someone else and go borrow from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a regular borrower. Even in that case, the כלי stays tied to the lender's feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that a lender who always lends to this person has him in mind before יום טוב, so the כלי should follow the borrower. The משנה teaches that it does not, because the lender is never sure this person will come to him this time. Since the lender did not settle on handing it over before יום טוב, the כלי stays with the lender's feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to doing something, a regular habit
'He surely says to himself.' The גמרא describes what the person is thinking

steps.whatToRemember: What decides is whether the lender settled on handing the כלי to the borrower before יום טוב. A loan agreed on before יום טוב follows the borrower. A loan made on יום טוב follows the lender, even if the borrower borrows from him regularly.
steps.confusionAlert: Being a regular borrower is not the same as having agreed on the loan before יום טוב. Only an actual agreement before יום טוב moves the כלי to the borrower's feet.

phrases.english: where he regularly borrows from him.
he places it in his possession,
phrases.notes: Meaning the lender, knowing his regular borrower, already thinks of the כלי as the borrower's before יום טוב.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will find another person
and go and borrow from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a less obvious case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lender who always lends to this person has already set the כלי aside for him, so it should follow the borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lender is not sure this person will come to him, so he does not hand the כלי over ahead of time, and it follows the lender's feet.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A loan made on יום טוב follows the lender, even with a regular borrower.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה: a woman who borrows from her friend
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a woman who borrowed food ingredients from her friend. The משנה rules that these follow the limits of both women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a woman who borrowed from her friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line of the משנה to start a new discussion. This sets up the story and question that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה says that if a woman borrows spices for a dish, or water and salt for her dough, the food follows the תחום of both women. The food may only be carried where both women are allowed to walk. This is the line the sages will soon question.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly. It links this case to the earlier cases in the משנה.
The area around a person or object within which it may be carried on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.notes: The משנה continues: spices for a dish, or water and salt for dough. These follow the limits of both women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the line about a borrowed כלי (steps 10-11) to the next line of the משנה, about borrowed ingredients.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ingredients a woman borrows from her friend (spices for a dish, water and salt for dough) follow the תחום of both women.

steps.title: רבי אבא arrives in ארץ ישראל and finds the sages discussing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא prays that his teaching will be accepted when he goes up to ארץ ישראל. He arrives and finds a group of sages in the middle of a discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבא went up to ארץ ישראל, he said: May it be God's will that I say something that will be accepted. When he went up, he found רבי יוחנן, רבי חנינא בר פפי and רבי זירא. Some say he found רבי אבהו, רבי שמעון בן פזי and רבי יצחק נפחא. They were sitting and saying:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that sets the scene. It is getting ready for the question the sages will ask and for רבי אבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא was a newcomer from בבל and wanted his first teaching to be accepted by the great sages of ארץ ישראל. The גמרא gives two versions of which sages he found, but the story continues the same way in both. Their discussion is about our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up. Used for moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Abba went up, he said:
phrases.notes: "Went up" means he moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: that I say a statement that will be accepted.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי וְרַבִּי זֵירָא
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Zeira,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
and they were sitting and saying:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the story in which the sages discuss the משנה line just quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It sets the scene: רבי אבא arrives and finds the sages of ארץ ישראל discussing our משנה.

steps.title: Why don't the water and salt become nullified in the dough?
steps.stepSummary: The sages ask why the dough should follow the lender's limits at all. The small amount of water and salt should just be nullified in the dough. רבי אבא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let the water and salt be nullified in the dough! רבי אבא said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The sages challenge the משנה's ruling about dough. Then the גמרא sets up רבי אבא's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small ingredient mixed into a much larger food becomes בטל, meaning it no longer counts on its own. The flour belongs to the woman who made the dough, so the dough should follow only her. Why should the borrowed water and salt drag it into the friend's limits too?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be nullified (become בטל, no longer counted on its own)
In relation to, inside (the larger mixture)

steps.confusionAlert: The sages are not saying the borrowing doesn't matter in general. They are asking only about water and salt, which are small additions mixed into a lot of flour.

phrases.notes: Meaning: why does the משנה say the dough follows both women?

phrases.english: Let the water and salt be nullified

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that dough made with borrowed water and salt follows the limits of both women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water and salt are minor ingredients that should become בטל in the much larger amount of flour. If so, the dough should follow only the owner of the flour.
